transcript:
This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Lynda Kenyon.
Democrats have seized the largest House majority since the 1990s,
now that a race in North Carolina has been called,
and that number could still grow.
NPR's Eric McDaniel has more.
The Associated Press says Democrat Chuck Hubbard
has ousted Republican incumbent Virginia Fox.
He'll represent the northwest corner of the state near Greensboro.
It's a notable win, not just because Fox was an 83-year-old committee chair
who'd been in Washington more than 20 years,
but also because it puts the running tally of Democratic House seats at 258,
matching the high watermark for either party that stretches back to the 1992 election.
And there are still a handful of races left to call.
It could push their majority even higher.
Democrats also have a commanding Senate majority
that will need to work with President Trump to get things signed into law.
Eric McDaniel and PR News in Washington.
The states of Virginia and Oregon are suing Elon Musk's AI company, SpaceX Superintelligence,
over concerns of sexually explicit images of women and children
made by users of its platform.
NPR's Wau-Jin Yang has the story.
This is the first time state governments are suing the company,
which makes chatbot Grok over deepfake sexualized images.
Like last year and earlier this year, Grok users altered photographs of a large number of people,
mostly women and sometimes children, depicting them in little to no clothing.
Although the company has since put in more guardrails, similar incidents have continued to happen.
Here's Oregon Attorney General Dan Rayfield.
When Congress doesn't act, we're forced as AGs to use the tools that we have to hold the line
and force compliance with our existing laws.
Using state consumer protection laws,
Virginia and Oregon accuse the company of both misrepresenting the risk of non-consensual sexual imagery
posed by its chatbot and exposing users to such images on social media platform X.
Huo-Jin Yang, NPR News.
The lawyer for the father and daughter pulled from a crowded Sea-Tac Airport jetway
by ICE agents over the weekend says they were here legally.
Kate Stone from member station KUOW has the latest.
Now viral video shows agents wrestling Ricardo Lorondo Mendoza and Sofia Hernandez Meija to the floor
while they were trying to board an Alaska Airlines flight on Saturday.
Homeland Security says both overstayed visas and Meija will face a felony charge for allegedly throwing hot coffee.
But their attorney Olia Catala says both hold valid work permits
and are allowed to live in the U.S. while awaiting pending asylum and green card decisions.
Congress created these legal pathways, Sofia and her father were using them.
Washington Governor Bob Ferguson says state officials are reviewing whether agents violated a state law passed in March
banning law enforcement officers from wearing masks.
For NPR News, I'm Kate Stone in Seattle.
You're listening to NPR News.
A new survey from Sesame Workshop finds families of young children say their kids are kind,
even as they overwhelmingly see the world as a very unkind place.
NPR's Corey Turner has the story.
The education nonprofit behind Sesame Street has twice surveyed American families about kindness in 2016 and now a decade later.
And the differences are striking.
This national sample of caregivers of kids ages three to eight saw a big increase in families who say kindness is just not a priority for most people.
And they gave Americans a pretty middling rating for kindness, 2.8 out of 5.
But compared to a decade ago, kids earned higher marks for kindness and resilience and they were less likely to be considered anxious.
Caregivers themselves were also much more likely in 2026 to say they value empathy in their kids over manners.
Corey Turner, NPR News.
Rockstar Games reports Grand Theft Auto VI has generated a record $3.79 billion in its first day of retail sales.
The game, which launched last Thursday, is the first new installment in the Grand Theft Auto series in 13 years.
Rockstar also reports selling 32.5 million units in pre-release.
The launch far surpasses that of GTA V, which made $1 billion in its first three days.
It came out in 2013.
This latest installment focuses on relationship building alongside the usual mayhem fans have come to expect.
I'm Linda Kenyon, NPR News in Washington.

topics.text: Democrat Chuck Hubbard ousts Republican Virginia Fox in North Carolina House race, giving Democrats 258 seats
Virginia and Oregon sue Elon Musk's SpaceX Superintelligence over sexualized deepfake images made by Grok
Lawyer says father and daughter pulled from Sea-Tac Airport jetway by ICE were in the U.S. legally
Sesame Workshop survey finds families see kids as kind but view the world as unkind
Rockstar Games reports Grand Theft Auto VI earned record $3.79 billion in first day of retail sales
